_about: Skills the Warden can learn from a trainer for coins. `craft`: a skill with recipes (recipes.json) names its crafting window, the verb in the log, its button and where you must stand. `teaches`: abilities that appear in the spellbook once learned. `maxRank`: skills that improve with use (each mined ore, butchered carcass or cooked dish that is not yet easy for you has a chance to raise them). `train` (a skill on the profession ladder): the trainer ranks past Novice, each { rank, trainer, cost, level (skill level needed), quest? (must be done) }. A laddered skill runs from 1 to 60 and its trainer rank caps it (`ladder.ranks`); it rises a point at a time, each successful task having a chance by its colour (`ladder.pointChance`, the same for every skill), and each level-up pays `ladder.charXpShare` of a character level's experience. `perks`: at each listed skill level you choose one of two; `effect` keys are read by the profession's system.

skills.name: Camping
skills.desc: Pitch a camp anywhere quiet. Your spirit rises there if you fall, resting by it builds rested experience, and Return to Camp brings you back to it.

skills.name: Fishing
skills.desc: Cast a line into still water and strike when the bob dips. Every water has a level: you need that much Fishing to fish it, and it teaches you less once it is easy. Better rods need more skill to use.

choices.name: Steady Hands
choices.desc: +10% chance to land a fish when you strike.

choices.name: Double Haul
choices.desc: 15% chance to land two fish at once.

choices.name: Deep Lure
choices.desc: Rare fish bite twice as often.

skills.name: Lockpicking
skills.desc: Open locked chests without their key (you need lockpicks). Each lock needs a certain rank; every lock you pick raises it.

skills.name: Cooking
skills.desc: Cook fish and meat at a fire (a camp or the inn's hearth). Grilled perch and roast dace come with the skill; Hester teaches more as you improve. Rises as you cook.

craft.station: a fire: your camp or a hearth

skills.name: Herbalism
skills.desc: Pick the herbs that grow wild across the land. Each herb has a level: you need that much Herbalism to pick it, and the best grow in dangerous places. Herbs move: a picked patch is gone, and another springs up nearby. A knife or sickle in your bags makes you quicker.

choices.name: Green Thumb
choices.desc: 25% chance to pick an extra herb.

choices.name: Rootcutter
choices.desc: Twice the chance of a herb's rare find (seeds, roots, the odd lost trinket).

choices.name: Healer's Touch
choices.desc: Picking a herb heals you for 4% of your health.

skills.name: Alchemy
skills.desc: Brew herbs into draughts and elixirs at an alchemy bench. Draughts heal at once; an elixir raises a stat for a while (one elixir at a time). Briony teaches more recipes as you improve.

choices.name: Careful Measure
choices.desc: 15% chance to brew two from one set of herbs.

choices.name: The Last Drop
choices.desc: 10% chance a draught or elixir is not used up when you drink it.

skills.name: Hunting
skills.desc: Butcher the beasts you kill for their hides, pelts and meat, and fillet fish for the pot (you need a skinning knife). Loot the body first, then butcher it. Higher-level beasts need a higher rank (5 ranks a level), and better fish take more skill to fillet; every carcass and fish not yet easy for you has a chance to raise the skill. Small fish still cook whole: filleting gets more from them.

craft.station: a skinning knife on your tool belt

skills.name: Mining
skills.desc: Mine the ore veins that glint in rock outcrops (you need a mining pick). Veins move: a mined-out outcrop goes bare and another in the same group starts to glint. Harder rock needs a higher rank (5 ranks an ore level); the skill rises with every swing that is not yet easy for you. Smelting the ore into bars is Smithing's work.

skills.name: Smithing
skills.desc: Smelt ore into bars at a forge, then hammer the bars into nails, arrowheads and tool heads at the anvil. Each recipe has a level; it teaches you less once it is easy. Iren teaches it alongside Mining.

skills.name: Woodcutting
skills.desc: Fell trees for logs (you need a hatchet on your tool belt). Each kind of tree has a level: ash for anyone, oak and yew for the practised. A felled tree is gone, and another grows nearby. Logs feed Woodcraft and the forge's charcoal.

skills.name: Woodcraft
skills.desc: Shape logs at a workbench into everything wooden: arrow shafts, tool handles, staffs, wands and the shaped timber folk need for repairs. Each recipe has a level; it teaches you less once it is easy.

ladder._about: The profession ladder (game/systems/skills.gd). Ranks cap the skill. Every successful skilling action, in every skill, has pointChance[colour] of giving one skill point (Dan 2026-11-11). A task's colour comes from how far your skill is over the level it needs: under bands[0] orange, under bands[1] yellow, under bands[2] green, past that grey (nothing to learn); a skill's own `bands` overrides these. Each skill level-up gives charXpShare of a character level's experience at that level.

masteries._about: Weapon masteries (game/systems/skills.gd, shown under Combat in the Skills window; Dan 2026-11-11). Every landed swing or shot with a weapon type gives `xpPerHit` mastery experience to that type; a level needs xpBase + xpPerLevel x level, up to maxLevel. Masteries give NO power: their `milestones` are cosmetic (swing styles, weapon glows: names only for now) and titles (titles.json `requires` { mastery, level }). `types`: each weapon type's mastery name; an item's `weaponType` picks it, a main-hand weapon without one counts as `sword`.

milestones.text: A faint glow on your weapon (coming later)
